Former Apple design chief Jony Ive has long described the iPhone's design philosophy as "a piece of glass." It is widely believed that even though Ive left Apple years ago, the company still adheres to this goal, and Liquid Glass is the software design paving the way for Apple's next-generation hardware.

We have learned from multiple reports that the 20th anniversary edition iPhone may bring us closer to Apple's vision in many ways, and the latest news could be another piece of the puzzle……

Key Expectations

Earlier rumours suggested Apple might release a standalone 20th anniversary special edition iPhone, but more recent reports indicate that all the features designed to achieve the "all-glass" design will eventually come to the iPhone 19 Pro. To complicate matters further, some believe that to highlight the anniversary significance, Apple will skip the iPhone 19 name and call it the iPhone 20 Pro instead.

There is still some time before the launch, and related reports remain highly speculative, but the most anticipated design highlight is expected to be a display that curves towards the edges on all four sides, creating the illusion of a bezel-less screen.

It is almost certain that Apple will finally succeed in embedding the Face ID module under the screen this year, and the market also expects the front camera and speaker to be similarly hidden beneath the display.

Combining these elements will present a highly convincing "piece of glass" appearance.

Glass Back

Leaker Fixed Focus Digital recently revealed another element of the overall design: the back will return to glass material, replacing the aluminium alloy used in recent models.

A glass back will make the device more fragile, but it undoubtedly helps achieve the "piece of glass" design philosophy. In pursuit of a futuristic design, do you think this is an acceptable trade-off? Feel free to share your views in the comment section.
